findings.trigger: dynamic_cooldown_applicator(context.bot) raises a RuntimeError -> apply_dynamic_cooldowns_step's own except (RuntimeError) catches it, logs one ERROR line and returns normally (no exception propagates).
findings.suggestion: Either let the exception propagate (remove the local try/except, or re-raise after logging) so run_startup_sequence's aggregator can count and report it, or stop calling this a step of the aggregated sequence.

findings.trigger: log_port_diagnostics() raises RuntimeError or asyncio.TimeoutError -> run_port_diagnostics_step's own except catches it, logs one ERROR line and returns normally, the same pattern as F1.
findings.suggestion: Same as F1: let the exception reach run_startup_sequence's aggregator instead of swallowing it locally.

findings.trigger: update_docker_cache(logger) (called at :566, inside the inner try at :557-595) raises an exception that is neither docker.errors.DockerException/ValueError/TypeError/KeyError/AttributeError (all handled inside update_docker_cache itself) nor ImportError/AttributeError/RuntimeError/ValueError/TypeError/KeyError (the two except clauses at :583 and :595) -> it escapes the inner try, then also escapes the outer except (AttributeError, RuntimeError) at :607, so it is never logged by this function's own handlers; the worker thread dies, only the `finally` block runs (bg_refresh_running reset, 'stopped' logged at INFO, indistinguishable from a clean shutdown).
findings.suggestion: Catch broadly here as mech_decay_worker already does at :839 and :853 (its own comment explains this exact class of bug, review C41) - background_refresh_worker's comment at :583 claims parity ('Service dependency errors') but the except clauses stay narrow, unlike the twin it is modeled on.
findings.unsure_why: I could not see the exception types actually raised by build_docker_client, image_name_of or compose_project_of (not part of this section's source), so I cannot confirm a concrete exception type that would slip through all the listed except clauses. The self-healing behaviour (get_docker_containers_live restarts the worker on the next call via _refresh_worker_is_running) also limits the practical impact, so I could not tell whether this is an overlooked gap or an accepted one.

notes: Only 2 of the startup sequence's documented 'nine' steps (cooldowns.py, diagnostics.py) were in this section's source; run_startup_sequence itself (sequence.py) is sound and its docstring's stated purpose - one aggregated failure line at the end instead of many scattered ones - is exactly what F1/F2 undermine for their own steps. check_docker_connectivity (web_helpers.py:615) has no caller in this section's source, so I could not confirm how its boolean return or a raised exception from connectivity_service.check_connectivity() is used upstream; read the function itself and found no defect, verdict 'checked' reflects that. The apparent duplicate-filter concern in get_docker_containers_live's rate-limiting fast path (:281-282, returns the full cache without honoring container_name/MAX_CONTAINERS_DISPLAY) turned out to be unreachable with any populated cache - that branch is only reached while global_timestamp is still None, i.e. before the cache has ever been filled, so docker_cache['containers'] is always [] there; not filed as a finding.
